hints: Focus on what acid hydrolysis does to an ester, it splits the molecule at the C-O single bond next to the carbonyl.
Notice the left side of P is $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$, so that fragment will become a two-carbon carboxylic acid.
Add $\text{OH}$ to the acyl side and $\text{H}$ to the alkoxy side to complete the acid plus alcohol pair, then match the alcohol carbon skeleton.
walkthrough:
**Recall acid hydrolysis of esters**

Think of hydrolysis as adding water across the ester link. With dilute acid as catalyst, you always get a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol.

$$\text{RCOOR' + H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{dilute HCl}} \text{RCO}_2\text{H + R'OH}$$

**Split ester P into its two parts**

Look at $\text{CH}_3\text{C(=O)OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$. Break the $\text{C-O}$ single bond. The $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ part is the acyl part, the $\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$ part is the alkoxy part.

$$\text{P = CH}_3\text{C(=O)-} + \text{-OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$$

**Form the acid and the alcohol**

Add $\text{OH}$ to the acyl fragment to make the acid, and add $\text{H}$ to the alkoxy fragment to make the alcohol. That gives ethanoic acid and 3-methylbutan-1-ol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H and (CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$ is an acyl chloride, not a hydrolysis product. Dilute HCl does not convert the acid part into an acyl chloride, it gives the carboxylic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$.
options.B: Incorrect. This swaps the fragments. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is too short for the alcohol part, and $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ wrongly puts a carboxylic acid on the alcohol side.
options.C: Incorrect. Acid hydrolysis of an ester gives one acid and one alcohol, not two acids. The second formula $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is a carboxylic acid, but that fragment should be an alcohol.
options.D: Correct. The $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ side becomes ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, and the $\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$ side becomes the alcohol $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. This is exactly the acid plus alcohol pair from acid hydrolysis.
